name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: The France–Bund spread hovers around the 150bp Alert line: 156bp on 16 Nov, about 149bp implied on 18 Nov
state: ABC Bourse put the French 10-year yield at 4.95% and the Bund at 3.40% on 16 Nov, a spread of 156bp, down from a 176bp peak at the end of October. The French yield slipped to 4.85% on 18 Nov and fell back below 4.9% on 20 Nov (Trading Economics), while Italy's 10-year closed at 4.42% on 18 Nov, 106bp over Bunds (Soldionline), implying a French spread near 149bp that day. With the spread moving either side of 150bp and no second outlet confirming a sustained close above it, the Alert is unconfirmed and the level stays Watch; no failed G7 auction or emergency buying was found.
for_you: French government borrowing costs are near their highest in over a decade relative to Germany, which tends to feed into French mortgage and corporate borrowing rates. Italy's spread is well below its stress line.
rubric_hit: France–Bund spread around 150bp (156bp 16 Nov, ~149bp 18 Nov); 80–150bp Watch band, Alert above 150bp unconfirmed

sources.title: ABC Bourse — L'écart de taux se creuse entre la France et l'Allemagne

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
